Subject: Pilot billing: context amortization & rounding policy questions

Hi Lydia —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Before our pilot kickoff I'd like to confirm how we will account for a few edge cases in the billing examples you sent: specifically amortization of long context across multiple messages, per-request rounding quantum, and the interaction with seat/commit discounts. We want to ensure the invoice math you see in month one matches expectations.

Quick overview of what I'm proposing (happy to update):
- Session window: 24-hour session window for amortizing context (prefixes/KV reuse) unless you opt into a persistent session SKU.
- Rounding quantum: charges are applied in 16-token quanta for aggregated session accounting; individual per-call minimum is 10 tokens.
- Minimums: per-API call floor = 10 tokens; per-session minimum billing floor = 1,000 tokens for uncommitted pilots (can be waived under a pilot credit).

I attached a short spreadsheet with worked examples (pilot-proposal.xlsx). Below are three concrete scenarios with the proposed math so you can sanity-check. If these look good we can lock them into the pilot SOW and I can route a 30% pilot discount for months 1–6 (applies to metered token charges).

Scenario A — short burst (support bot quick reply)
- Request payload: prompt + user message = 45 tokens generated total
- Per-call floor: 10 tokens (apply) -> rounded up to 1 quantum? No, small calls above floor are billed as max(floor, tokens) then aggregated into 16-token quanta at invoice time. So: 45 tokens billed as 45 tokens immediately; session aggregation later groups remaining fractional quanta.
- Invoice math (no aggregation credit): 45 tokens -> rounded to 45 (measured) -> charged at token rate.

Scenario B — long context (multi-turn therapy assistant with 9,600 token context)
- Initial ingest: 9,600 tokens stored as context; generation per turn ~400 tokens on average
- Session amortization: 24-hr window treats the 9,600 context as amortized over requests that reuse the KV cache; invoice takes amortized cost per request = (context_tokens * context_unit_rate) / max(1, estimated_reuse_count). For our pilot we assume reuse_count=12 (roughly per-user daily interactions).
- Example: context amortized per turn = 9,600 / 12 = 800 tokens of context attributed per turn + 400 generated = 1,200 billable tokens per turn. Rounding quantum 16 applies to the per-turn total when producing invoice line items.

Scenario C — streaming + heartbeats + ephemeral prefixes
- Heartbeat small calls (10–20 token keepalive) qualify for KV preservation but are subject to the 10-token per-call floor. We do not count heartbeats toward amortization unless they trigger a cold start.
- Hybrid flows: if you opt into persistent session SKU, the context minimum per-session is reduced and amortization denominator increases (e.g., reuse_count -> 30) which lowers per-turn amortized context.

Discount & packaging options (proposal)
- Pilot credit: 30% off metered token charges for first six months (applies after aggregation and before seat/commit discounts).
- Commit option: 12-month reserved token bucket with 10% additional discount and included KV persistence (reduces amortization burden).
- If Meridian prefers simpler invoicing we can map to a seat + per-call overage: seat covers baseline KV cost and per-call token usage billed only for generations.

Next steps
1) Confirm the amortization approach (24h window vs persistent session SKU).
2) Decide whether we should waive the 1,000-token per-session minimum for pilot.
3) If confirmed, I will add language to the SOW and request the pilot discount approval from finance.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if you want to walk through the spreadsheet.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Lydia —

Thanks — attached is a short PDF with numeric examples (calculation-examples.pdf). Below are the headline answers to your three asks and a recommended smoothing path.

1) Numeric examples for 25 active users (one week) — headline numbers (see attached for full breakdown):
- Scenario A (support bot bursts): approx 25 users * 10 bursts/day * 45 tokens = 11,250 tokens -> billed raw = 11,250 -> after pilot discount (30%) = 7,875 tokens-equivalent billing value.
- Scenario B (long context amortized): 25 users * 20 turns/week * 1,200 amortized tokens = 600,000 tokens -> after aggregation/16-token quanta this becomes line items rounded up to nearest 16 tokens; post-discount = 420,000 tokens-equivalent billing value.
- Scenario C (hybrid streaming + heartbeats): heartbeats are negligible but floor applies; example week = 25 users * 7 heartbeats/day * 10 tokens = 1,750 tokens -> post-floor and aggregation = ~1,760 tokens -> post-discount = 1,232 tokens-equivalent billing value.

2) Rounding quantum: currently platform default is 16 tokens for session-level aggregation (we chose 16 because it aligns with our compression kernels and amortization buckets). It is configurable for enterprise contracts; for pilots we can keep 16 but commit to presenting an invoice preview before month-end so Meridian can flag anything unexpected.

3) Month-one smoothing: recommended path
- Waive the 1,000-token per-session minimum for pilot and instead apply a hard month-one cap equal to 120% of forecasted pilot usage (per the attached examples). If forecast is exceeded we will notify and apply overage at the agreed pilot rate.

If you prefer, Jordan can join a short call to walk the calculations and show a mock invoice.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
